Accessible October 2024 paper documenting adverse employment effects on a freelance platform.
University repository supplies the findings, peer-review status, and publication date of a substantial counterexample involving freelance demand.

evidence_items.publisher: Becker Friedman Institute, University of Chicago
evidence_items.locator: Abstract; supporting discussion in section 4.4, Comparison to the Literature
evidence_items.explanation: The study covers 11 exposed occupations in Denmark and finds no significant earnings or hours effects. Its literature discussion identifies narrow freelance markets as the closest existing displacement evidence; the event date marks this research entering the contemporary record.

evidence_items.publisher: American Economic Association; Xiang Hui, Oren Reshef, and Luofeng Zhou
evidence_items.locator: Introduction, paragraph reporting the main ChatGPT results
evidence_items.explanation: The paper reports fewer monthly contracts and lower earnings among more-exposed freelancers, so meaningful displacement research already existed. Its platform-specific scope does not establish broad labor-market displacement; the event date identifies the dated paper version.

evidence_items.publisher: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization; Oxford University Research Archive
evidence_items.locator: Abstract, final sentence; preceding sentences report demand changes
evidence_items.explanation: Teutloff and colleagues report a 20–50% relative decline in demand for substitutable freelance skills, alongside growth in some complementary work. This is material evidence of concentrated displacement pressure, but job postings on one platform do not measure broad realized worker displacement.

unresolved_gaps: The search is not an exhaustive systematic review of every study available by publication.
The complete contemporary Oxford Economics report was not obtained.
No source-supplied threshold settles whether sizeable effects within a freelance platform count as 'at scale'.
